searched: Searched on 29 October 2026 for acqui-hire and licensing-plus-hiring arrangements of 2023-2026 not yet in the dataset: Amazon-Covariant (aboutamazon.com, covariant.ai, GeekWire), Meta-Scale AI (Scale AI's announcement), regulator texts on the existing deals (gov.uk CMA case pages for Microsoft/Inflection; web searches for CMA or FTC case pages on Amazon-Adept, Google-Character.AI, Amazon-Covariant, NVIDIA-Groq), NVIDIA-Groq (groq.com newsroom, CNBC), NVIDIA-Enfabrica (CNBC), Anthropic and the Humanloop team (humanloop.com, TechCrunch), Google DeepMind and Hume AI (hume.ai blog, TechCrunch, HIT Consultant, The Decoder), and Meta's 2025 founder hires. Covariant's own blog post on the Amazon agreement could not be retrieved: covariant.ai now serves a placeholder page and the post's address returns 404, so Covariant's leadership change rests on GeekWire's report of that post. No Hume AI or Google text on the Hume agreement and no Enfabrica or NVIDIA text on the Enfabrica agreement was found; those records rest on reporting. Wired, which first reported the Hume agreement, is not reachable through the search tool and was not retrieved. No CMA or FTC case page or decision was found for Amazon-Adept, Google-Character.AI, Amazon-Covariant or NVIDIA-Groq; the FTC chair's January 2026 remarks on acqui-hires were reported from a television interview and are not a decision on a named deal.

claims.subject: microsoft
claims.statement: The UK Competition and Markets Authority's decision of 4 September 2024 (full text published on 24 October 2024) describes the transaction as the acquisition by Microsoft of certain assets of Inflection AI, which it found to be a relevant merger situation, and calls the assets acquired the 'Target Enterprise'.

time.note: The CMA states that the Transaction completed and was made public on 19 March 2024 (para 132); its decision was given on 4 September 2024.

attributes.scope: Certain assets of Inflection AI (the CMA's 'Target Enterprise'), not Inflection AI as a company

claims.qualification: The regulator’s characterisation for merger-control purposes: an acquisition of certain assets (the hired team and associated arrangements, including a non-exclusive licence), not of Inflection AI as a company; the CMA records Microsoft’s account that the remaining Inflection business pivoted towards a B2B (enterprise) business. Microsoft and Inflection did not describe the arrangement as an acquisition in the sources recorded. The CMA found no realistic prospect of a substantial lessening of competition.

evidence.passage: the transaction described below involving the acquisition by Microsoft Corporation (Microsoft) of certain assets of Inflection AI, Inc. (Inflection), is a relevant merger situation
The CMA considers Microsoft to be the ‘Acquirer’, and those assets acquired by Microsoft as a result of the Transaction as the ‘Target Enterprise’.
Microsoft also entered into a series of arrangements with Inflection including, among others, a non-exclusive licensing deal to utilise Inflection IP in a range of ways.
The Transaction completed and was made public on 19 March 2024.
the remaining Inflection business pivoted towards a B2B (enterprise) business

claims.subject: nvidia
claims.statement: Groq announced on 24 December 2025 that it had entered into a non-exclusive licensing agreement with Nvidia for Groq’s inference technology, under which its founder Jonathan Ross, its president Sunny Madra and other members of the Groq team would join Nvidia, and that Groq would continue to operate as an independent company.

time.note: Announcement date; not a closing or effective date.

claims.qualification: Groq's announcement of a licence and of hiring; it discloses no terms. CNBC reported the same day that an investor in Groq described the deal as a purchase of assets for about $20 billion; NVIDIA's CEO wrote in an internal email, as CNBC reported it, that NVIDIA was not acquiring Groq as a company. The record does not record an acquisition.

evidence.passage: Groq states that it has entered into a non-exclusive licensing agreement with Nvidia for its inference technology; that as part of the agreement Jonathan Ross, Groq's founder, Sunny Madra, its president, and other team members will join Nvidia to advance and scale the licensed technology; and that Groq will continue as an independent company.

evidence.locator: Paragraph quoting Jensen Huang's email to employees
evidence.passage: While we are adding talented employees to our ranks and licensing Groq’s IP, we are not acquiring Groq as a company.
